title: Fix typos and unclear sentences in the Session 1 notes
body:
## Problem
The Session 1 notes may contain typos or sentences that a first-year student finds confusing.

## Context
Beginners judge the whole repo by Session 1.

## Expected outcome
A clearer `sessions/session-01/README.md` and `lesson.py` comments.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-01/README.md`, `sessions/session-01/lesson.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At least three improvements
- [ ] `python start.py test` still passes

## Difficulty
beginner

title: Add a second law to Session 1: a cooling cup of tea
body:
## Problem
Session 1 only uses the falling ball; students would benefit from a second example with an exponential shape.

## Context
Newton's cooling law gives an exponential decay; the candidate library has no exponential decay yet.

## Expected outcome
A short extra section in `lesson.py` with synthetic cooling data and a candidate `c * exp(-t)`, plus one checkpoint line.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-01/lesson.py`, `sessions/session-01/checkpoint.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The new check passes
- [ ] A figure with labelled axes and units

## Difficulty
beginner

title: Add nonlinear constant fitting (Session 4)
body:
## Problem
The shipped search fits only the constants a and b outside the formula, so y = 5 x / (1 + 0.37 x) cannot be recovered.

## Context
See `promo/roadmap.md`, milestone 1.

## Expected outcome
`sessions/session-04/` with README (sections A to F), lesson, checkpoint, exercises and app in the same style as Sessions 1 to 3.

## Relevant files
`promo/roadmap.md`, `sessions/session-03/lesson.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Checkpoint prints PASS and the roadmap checkpoint is met
- [ ] Added to the tests

## Difficulty
intermediate

title: Support two input variables in the enumeration
body:
## Problem
`enumerate_pool` takes one input array x. Many laws have two inputs (for example concentration and temperature).

## Context
Roadmap milestone 2.

## Expected outcome
A version that takes a matrix of inputs, with duplicates removed, and a checkpoint recovering r = x1 sqrt(x2).

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-03/lesson.py`, `promo/roadmap.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At least 90 percent recovery at 5 percent noise
- [ ] Runtime reported

## Difficulty
intermediate

title: Reproduce the Target: a genetic search that rediscovers the pendulum law
body:
## Problem
The Target animation shows a genetic search; there is no public implementation.

## Context
The code behind the Target is private on purpose. The roadmap gives the path.

## Expected outcome
Your own implementation, written from the roadmap, plus an animation like the Target.

## Relevant files
`promo/roadmap.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Recovers the pendulum law from noisy data
- [ ] Short write-up of your method

## Difficulty
advanced

title: Translate the Session 1 notes into Hindi
body:
## Problem
Students who prefer Hindi cannot read Session 1 comfortably.

## Context
This project teaches first- and second-year students across India; translations widen who can join.

## Expected outcome
`sessions/session-01/README.hi.md` with a faithful Hindi translation of sections A to F, linked from the main README.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-01/README.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All sections translated
- [ ] Equations, code blocks and file names unchanged
- [ ] Link added to the main README

## Difficulty
beginner
